issues: period: the detail is register administration from 1787 to 1893 - the Revolution name and the 1868 and 1893 absorptions with their component streets - and the summary already says the street absorbed its neighbours in 1868 and 1893. The one part that bears on the map, the rue des Poulies names, is a list of four variants.
suggested_edit: Cut the 1868 and 1893 sentences, which the summary covers, and give the room to the Poulies names and what they meant. If nothing can be said about them, the register entry does not support a detail.

issues: period: the last two sentences are the 1885 transfer. | consistency: this card is probably a second label on the same street as L0238 and carries a near-identical list of names, so the site says the same thing twice. | voice: a list of eight former names and an administrative order.
suggested_edit: Return null. The card's own point - that the map seems to label one street twice, and that Guillot called it simply the rue du Temple - is in the summary, and a second copy of L0238's name list adds nothing.

issues: period: the closing sentence is a March 2017 municipal naming of a section as passage Walter Benjamin. | consistency: the name series 1233-1430 largely restates the summary, which already gives the 1233 Ecofle and the evolution through Escoufle and Escoufles into Ecouffes; the dates are the addition.
suggested_edit: Cut the 2017 sentence and keep the dated series, which is the new part.

issues: period: 47 of the entry's 78 words are a municipal decision of June 2019 naming part of the street after Pierre Seel. | consistency: the rue des Juifs name and the 13th-century date are both in the summary; the one fact it adds is that the street was earlier the rue des Rosiers - which is the name of the neighbouring street on card L0242, a shared name the author states flatly and should have flagged.
suggested_edit: Cut the 2019 sentence. And note the clash: "earlier still the rue des Rosiers" needs saying beside the fact that the rue des Rosiers is the next street over and has its own card.

issues: source: "rue Bouquetonne" is listed among the street's 14th-century names, but the register gives it as "rue Bouquetonne (Truschet)" - a citation of THIS map, which the card's own short description correctly reports as "this map labels [it] separately as the rue Bouquetonne". The detail drops the attribution, so a reading taken off this woodcut is presented as a medieval attestation. | voice: 141 words, the longest entry in the set, consisting of nothing but name variants.
suggested_edit: "...rue du Hoqueton or Hoqueton le Faucheur in the 14th century, and rue Bouquetonne on this map." Then cut the Croix Blanche list to two or three names: at 141 words the entry has room for something that is not a name.

issues: overclaim: "The mapmaker Lacaille" - the source says only "Lacaille", and Jean de La Caille was a printer-bookseller who published a plan, not a mapmaker; the trade is the detail's own addition. | period: six of the seven dates are 1768, 1793, 1806 and 1808; the 14th-century name and the 1328 ruelle au Villain, which are the map-relevant part, get one clause each.
evidence: data.bnf.fr, authority record for Jean de La Caille (1645-1723), https://data.bnf.fr/12192872/jean_de_la_caille/fr.pdf: he is recorded as an imprimeur-libraire who succeeded Denis II Thierry as printer-bookseller to the police in 1712, and the Description de la ville et des fauxbourgs de Paris en vingt planches (1714) is listed under him in that capacity. So "Lacaille" in the street register is an authority who published a plan in twenty plates, which is not the same as being its maker.
suggested_edit: "Lacaille writes rue Courtauvillain, and rue or ruelle Auvillain" - give him no trade. Lead on the 1328 ruelle au Villain and the rue du Seigneur de Montmorency, and compress the 1768-1808 renamings into one clause.

issues: consistency: the card is the rue de l'Homme-Arme and it gets one sentence; the other five are the rue des Deux Portes, the rue des Billettes and the rue du Chaume group. The armed man's shop sign, which is the card's own subject, is in the summary and is never picked up. | overclaim: "rue des Jardins in the 13th century" drops the source's "a la fin du".
suggested_edit: Give the card's street the body of the text, and name the others only as the neighbouring sections they are: "The rue de l'Homme-Arme ran between the rue Sainte-Croix-de-la-Bretonnerie and the rue des Blancs-Manteaux; the sections joined to it to the south had been the rue des Deux Portes, known as rue Entre Deux Portes in the late 13th century, and the rue des Billettes, the rue des Jardins at the same date."

issues: period: two of the three sentences are a 1957 transfer of 37 metres to the Ecole Polytechnique and a 1995 absorption of the cul-de-sac into the rue Jacques-Henri-Lartigue. The 16th-century names rue du Puits and rue du Champ Gaillard, which are the map's own moment, get one clause.
suggested_edit: Keep the first sentence and cut the other two. "In the 16th century it was also the rue du Puits and the rue du Champ Gaillard" is the whole of what this card needs.

issues: consistency: the two sections, the rue Neuve-Saint-Laurent name and the demolition for the rue de Turbigo are all in the summary; the detail's additions are one variant, rue Gaillardbois, and the exact 1865 decree. It also drops the 1546 attestation, which is the card's point: the street was new when the map was made.
suggested_edit: "The street existed in 1546 and was also called the rue Gaillardbois." That is the entry.

issues: voice: 62 words of nothing but former names, none of them dated, including two 19th-century ones (impasse du Roi de Rome, rue de Rome). Nothing is said about the street or the maire of Saint-Martin-des-Champs it is named after.
suggested_edit: Return null. Where a register entry is a list of undated variants and the summary has already explained the name, there is no detail to write.

issues: source: the detail copies the register's bowdlerised entry as a street name - "rue Trace put...", ellipsis and all - which reads on the card as a broken word rather than a name. | source: the list of the rue Transnonain's names stops one short and never reaches "rue Transnonnain", the card's own name, which the source gives as the last of the series ("et enfin, rue Transnonnain"). | period: the closing sentence is the 1972 clearance for the Centre national d'art contemporain.
suggested_edit: Drop "rue Trace put..." rather than print a truncation, and close the series properly: "...rue Trousse Nonnain, rue Tasse Nonnain and at last rue Transnonnain." Cut the 1972 sentence. The opening - a street of the late 11th century crossing the city wall, called rue de la Poterne inside it and rue outre la Poterne Nicolas Hydron outside - is the best material here and should lead.

issues: period: the closing sentence is the 1972 clearance for the Centre national d'art contemporain, as at L0288. | consistency: the 1817 closure is in the summary.
suggested_edit: Cut the last sentence and the 1817 decree. The late-13th-century rue Aufroy des Gres with its Latin form, and the 1313 tax roll, are the right material and are well handled.

issues: consistency: the 1427 first mention and the southern section's old name are both in the summary. | voice: the closing sentence - "The dead-end section extending beyond the rue des Ecoles was later opened by the City of Paris" - has no date and says nothing a reader of a 1550 map can use.
suggested_edit: Cut the last sentence. "Saint-Nicolas pres du Puits" and the opening of about 1246 are the new facts and are worth keeping, with the hedge the detail rightly preserves.

issues: period: two of the four sentences are the 1865 and 1869 renamings of stretches into the rue Linne and the rue Jussieu. | consistency: the one period fact the register carries - that the street was already there when the abbey was founded - is dropped, and the register dates that foundation to the 11th century where the site's own summary and card L0049 say the 12th; the clash should have gone in notes.
suggested_edit: Keep the course from the rue Copeau to the place Maubert and the rue du Faubourg Saint-Victor name, cut the 1865 and 1869 sentences, and flag the 11th/12th-century clash to the maintainer rather than writing either date.

issues: overclaim: "During the Revolutionary era, from 1793 until 1815" - 1815 is the Restoration, and the source gives only the span, not a label for it.
suggested_edit: "It was simply the rue de la Montagne from 1793 to 1815." The 1266-1276 attestation is the useful new fact here and reads well.

issues: consistency: the card is the western stretch - its summary is the lord of Montmorency's street and Flamel's house - and the detail is entirely about the eastern stretch between the rue Beaubourg and the rue du Temple, which is the neighbouring card L0262; a reader is told "This eastern segment adopted the name rue de Montmorency in 1768" on a card whose own street carried that name from the 14th century. | overclaim: "the entire street was renamed the rue de la Reunion" - the source's "elle" is the eastern part under discussion, and the register does not say the whole street took the name. | overclaim: "The cartographer Lacaille", as at L0262.
evidence: data.bnf.fr, authority record for Jean de La Caille (1645-1723), https://data.bnf.fr/12192872/jean_de_la_caille/fr.pdf: imprimeur-libraire, printer-bookseller to the police from 1712, under whom the Description de la ville et des fauxbourgs de Paris en vingt planches (1714) is listed. The register's "Lacaille" is a published authority, not a cartographer. The split of the street is the register's own: "La partie situee entre les rues Saint-Martin et Beaubourg... rue du Seigneur de Montmorency. La partie situee entre les rues Beaubourg et du Temple... la ruelle au Villain."
suggested_edit: Write this card from its own stretch: "From the 14th century the part between the rue Saint-Martin and the rue Beaubourg was the rue du Seigneur de Montmorency, after the lord whose house stood on it." Then, if the eastern stretch is mentioned at all, say plainly that it is the neighbouring section. Cut "the entire street" and Lacaille's trade.

issues: voice: nine former names in 74 words and nothing else; the register's own list has rue du Maure twice and ends with it, and the detail quietly drops the first occurrence and adds "officially" to the last. | overclaim: "before it was officially named the rue du Maure" - the register says only "et enfin rue du Maure".
suggested_edit: Cut to the names that carry something - the 1313 tax roll's Jehan Palee, and the Poterne and Fausse Poterne that explain the engraver's slip the card's own note describes - and drop "officially".

issues: overclaim: "Quiquenpoit by Jacques Androuet du Cerceau, and Quinquempoix by Jean-Baptiste-Michel Jaillot" - the register writes only "(Ducerceau)" and "(Jaillot)". Both expansions turn out to be right, and both are corroborated inside this project's own corpus, so the fault is not the identification but the silent supplying of it: the brief asks for additions to be declared, not slipped in.
evidence: Both names are confirmed from sources this project already holds. For du Cerceau: data/places_streets.csv, note for L0356, "as on Ducerceau's plan of 1555", and the sources_long extracts for L0441 and L0442, "plan de Truschet et Hoyau et plan de Jacques Androuet du Cerceau dessines vers 1550". For Jaillot: the fr.wikipedia article "Couvent des Cordelieres (Paris)" (read 3 Nov 2026) cites "J.B.M. Renou de Chauvigne Jaillot, Recherches critiques : historiques et topographiques sur la ville de Paris, vol. 4, Lottin, 1779", and the "Filles-Dieu" article cites the same work as by "Jean-Baptiste Michel Jaillot" - the authority the street register means.
suggested_edit: Write "Ducerceau" and "Jaillot" as the register does, and put the full names in the card's sources, where a reader can see where they come from.

issues: overclaim: three additions the source does not make - "Henri" Sauval (the register says only "Sauval"), "the 16th-century map of the Tapisserie" (the register gives no date, and published datings of the plan de la Tapisserie range over c. 1540, 1547 and c. 1550, with the tapestry itself about 1571), and "briefly" of the 1851 designation. | voice: the street is called "the passage" in the third sentence, a word the source does not use.
evidence: No page on the plan de la Tapisserie was opened and read, so its dating is reported from catalogue descriptions seen in search results only (Princeton's facsimile record labels it 1547, a Merian caption c. 1540 with the tapestry c. 1571, a dealer listing c. 1550). The finding is that the source gives no date, not that 16th-century is wrong. Marked shallow for that reason.
suggested_edit: "Sauval claims it was once called the rue du Croc; the plan de la Tapisserie gives it the name la Radrerie." Drop "Henri", "16th-century", "briefly" and "passage".

issues: voice: the entry opens "The list of former names recorded for the street is extensive", which tells the reader about the source rather than about the street, and then gives the list. | consistency: the rue de la Vieille-Oreille and the rue Guillori are in the summary, and the 1564 widening - the card's one fact from the map's own decade - is left there too.
suggested_edit: "Widened in 1564, the cutlers' street had been the rue des Recommanderesses, the rue de la Vieille Oreille or Guigne Oreille, and the rue Guillori." Drop the opening sentence.

issues: period: "the place de l'Hotel-de-Ville" on a card about 1550, where the card's own summary says place de Greve; the register uses the modern name and the detail follows it. | consistency: the 1252 naming and the avenue Victoria clearance are in the summary. The 16th-century rue des Recommanderesses is the useful new fact and is buried third.
suggested_edit: "From the place de Greve to the rue Saint-Martin..." and lead on the 16th-century name: by the time of this map the end towards the rue Saint-Martin was the rue des Recommanderesses.

issues: overclaim: "the 17th-century historian Henri Sauval" - the register says only "Sauval dit". Both the forename and the century are supplied, as at L0319 and L0349; the site does assert them elsewhere (L0410's summary calls him "Henri Sauval, a 17th-century historian of Paris"), but not in this source. | period: the place is called "place de l'Hotel-de-Ville" where the card's own summary uses its 1550 name, the place de Greve, and the same slip is at L0322. | consistency: the clearance for the avenue Victoria is in the summary.
suggested_edit: "Sauval says it was once called the ruelle de la Planche aux Teinturiers." Use "place de Greve" on a card about 1550, and cut the closing sentence.

issues: voice: "it was incorporated into the expanded expanse of the place du Parvis Notre-Dame". | consistency: the 1163 building, the extent and the absorption into the parvis are all in the summary; the additions are the late-13th-century name and the Revolution's rue de la Raison.
suggested_edit: "...until it was taken into the enlarged parvis." And lead on the one new fact that bears on the map: by the end of the 13th century it was the rue Neuve-Notre-Dame.

issues: consistency: the detail contains no fact the short description does not already carry - the course between the rue de la Bucherie and the rue Galande, the names rue du Pave de la place Maubert and rue d'Amboise, and the 1806-1912 merger are all in the summary. | overclaim: "before being separated again and subsequently given its modern designation" is an inference the register does not state.
suggested_edit: Return null. The register entry is three sentences and the summary has spent all three.

issues: source: the extract supplied is the register entry for the BOULEVARD SAINT-GERMAIN - a list of the twenty-odd streets the boulevard swallowed - and the card is the rue des Noyers. The detail is therefore wholly about the 19th-century boulevard that destroyed the street, and nothing in it can be trimmed to leave anything about the street the map shows. | overclaim: "dozens of ancient Left Bank streets and alleys" is a count the register does not give; it names about twenty-five items.
suggested_edit: Return null for this source, and source the rue des Noyers from its own entry. The register's boulevard Saint-Germain entry is the wrong document for any of the streets it lists.

issues: source: the register line the last sentence rests on is truncated - "Actuellement pas. Du Clos Bruneau pour la partie restante", almost certainly "impasse du Clos-Bruneau" - and the detail repairs it into "a surviving stub, which retains the name of Clos Bruneau" without saying that the source is broken. | consistency: the 1243 rue Judas and the boulevard Saint-Germain destruction are both in the summary.
suggested_edit: Either say plainly that what remains is the impasse du Clos-Bruneau, if that can be confirmed, or stop after the 1243 name.

issues: period: the text closes on a 1974 extension of the place Alphonse-Laveran in front of a military hospital, on a card about the cardo of Lutetia and the road to Compostela. | voice: "this major Left Bank arterial road" is traffic-engineering English; and the list of grand'rue names stops before reaching "grand'rue Saint-Jacques", which the source gives as the last of the series.
suggested_edit: Cut the 1974 clause, write "this great Left Bank street", and close the list where the source does: "...grand'rue vers Saint-Matelin, grand'rue Saint-Benoit, and at last grand'rue Saint-Jacques."

issues: overclaim: "Jean Boisseau" - the register says only "Boisseau", and the first name is the detail's addition, the same habit as Lacaille, Sauval and Ducerceau elsewhere in this set.
suggested_edit: Write "Boisseau". Otherwise this entry is sound: the hedge on Jean le Maitre is kept, the names are in order, and the Cholets college's own street is the subject throughout.

issues: consistency: the summary already says the rue du Renard-Saint-Sauveur and the rue Beaurepaire were joined to it in 1868, and the detail opens with that merger and then spends two of its three sentences on those two streets rather than on the rue d'Arnetal the card is about. | period: the opening sentence is the 1868 order.
suggested_edit: Open on the card's own street: "Earlier forms of the name run rue d'Arnetal, Darnetal, Dernetat, Drenetat and Darnestat, and it was also called the rue de la Trinite." Then the two absorbed streets in one sentence each, with their 1255 and 1313 dates.

issues: overclaim: "the 17th-century plan of Blondel" - the register says only "Sur le plan de Blondel"; the century is supplied. | consistency: the summary gives the later name as the rue du Petit-Hurleur, on Cousin's authority, and the detail gives "rue du Petit Leu" from the register, with nothing to tell a reader that these are two sources differing about the same street.
suggested_edit: "On Blondel's plan it is the rue du Petit Leu." And say that Cousin's rue du Petit-Hurleur and the register's rue du Petit Leu are two readings of the same street, which is worth more than either on its own.

issues: consistency: the 13th-century existence and the extent between the rue Saint-Martin and the rue Saint-Denis are in the summary, as is the goose etymology; the detail's additions are three spellings and an 1881 transfer of a section to the rue Etienne-Marcel. | voice: "Its name evolved from earlier spellings" presents a list of names the register gives as alternatives as a line of descent.
suggested_edit: "It appears as the rue As Oues, aux Oues and aux Oes." Cut the 1881 sentence.

issues: overclaim: the register hedges the Pourpointerie - "une partie de cette voie AURAIT ETE denommee rue de la Pourpointerie en 1612 et 1636" - and the detail states it flatly ("A portion of it is recorded as"). The second hedge, on rue Alain de Dampierre, is kept, so the two are treated differently in one sentence. | overclaim: "Henri Sauval" for the register's "Sauval".
suggested_edit: "A part of it is said to have been called the rue de la Pourpointerie in 1612 and 1636", and "Sauval".

issues: overclaim: "it was briefly renamed as part of the rue des Ecrivains" - "briefly" is the detail's addition, as at L0319 and L0367, all three on the same kind of 1851 register line.
suggested_edit: "A prefectoral order of 11 March 1851 made it part of the rue des Ecrivains." The 1300 Hiaumerie with the source's own gloss on heaume is well done.

issues: consistency: the soap-makers, the early-14th-century name and the destruction by the rue de Rivoli are all in the summary; the only new fact is which two streets it ran between.
suggested_edit: Return null. Three sentences of register, two of them already spent on the card.

issues: overclaim: "the 16th-century plan of Jacques Androuet du Cerceau" and "the adjoining rue du Chevalier-du-Guet" - the register says only "d'apres le plan de Ducerceau" and does not say the two streets adjoin. The identification is sound within this project, which dates that plan 1555 on the neighbouring card L0356, but it is not in this source.
suggested_edit: "On Ducerceau's plan this street and the rue du Chevalier-du-Guet both carry the name rue de la Serpente."

issues: consistency: the detail contains no fact the short description does not already have - the early-13th-century date, the run down to the river, and the 1912 renaming of the southern end to rue Edouard-Colonne are all in it. What it adds is the exact decree date and two boundary streets.
suggested_edit: Return null. The register entry is two sentences and the summary has both.

issues: overclaim: "The cartographer Lacaille" adds a trade the register does not give (see L0262); "it was originally called the rue Macra Madiana" hardens the source's conditional "elle se serait appelee", and adds "originally"; "later recorded it as" adds a sequence the register does not give. | period: the closing two clauses are the 1806 and 1814 renamings, and the 1786 edict on the riverside houses - the one thing here about the street as a place - is left to the summary.
suggested_edit: "Older deeds are said to have called it the rue Macra Madiana; Lacaille names it the rue de la Vieille Pelleterie, a name it already bore in 1183." Cut the Desaix renaming.

issues: source: the register derives the name Calande, attested "des 1280", from a house that belonged to Jean de la Kalendre in 1343 - sixty years after the name it is supposed to explain. The detail passes the impossibility on as an alternative etymology without flagging it, where the brief asks for it in notes.
suggested_edit: "By 1280 it was the rue de la Calande; the register connects the name with a house of Jean de la Kalendre, though it dates that house to 1343, after the name." Or drop the etymology and keep the 13th-century descriptive names, which are the better material.

issues: consistency: the summary already gives Eremburge de Brie and the corruption into Bout-de-Brie and Boutebrie; the detail is the same etymology retold with the Latin form and five more spellings, and it leaves the 14th-century street of the illuminators to the summary.
suggested_edit: Keep the Latin Eremburgis de Bria and two or three spellings, and let the rest go.

issues: voice: a list of former names; the one thing in it that bears on the map - "several 16th-century maps label it rue Serpente" - is buried mid-sentence and is the best line in the entry. | consistency: the summary already gives the 1179 opening, the 1180 vicus Serpentis and the 1851 absorption of the rue du Battoir.
suggested_edit: Lead on the map: "Several 16th-century plans, this one among them, write it rue Serpente; a deed of 1263 has the Latin Vicus Tortuosus, the winding street." Then the Battoir names, shorter.

issues: overclaim: "Briefly designated as part of the rue des Noyers" - "briefly" added, as at L0319 and L0350. | voice: "prefectural decree" for arrete prefectoral; the house form elsewhere in the set is "prefectoral".
suggested_edit: "Made part of the rue des Noyers by a prefectoral decree of 10 May 1851, it was destroyed soon after by the boulevard Saint-Germain." The 1383 rue aux Moines de Cernay is the good fact here.

issues: voice: the Latin "vicus Cithare in Judearia (1247)" is quoted without the two names that make it legible - the register says that section "etait rue de la Juiverie et rue de la Vieille Juiverie" - so a reader meets "in Judearia" with nothing to attach it to.
suggested_edit: "Between the rue Saint-Severin and the rue de l'Ecole-de-Medecine it was the rue de la Juiverie, vicus Cithare in Judearia in 1247 and vicus Harpe in 1270."

issues: period: both sentences are after the map - the 1792 rue Catinat, the return in 1802, and a 1934 absorption into the place Paul-Painleve. Everything the register has from before 1550, the 13th-century rue des Deux-Portes, the rue Sorbonne of about 1281 and Guillot's rue aux Hoirs de Sabonnes, is in the summary and the detail steps over all of it. | voice: 42 words, at the floor, of register administration.
suggested_edit: Return null. Once the summary has taken the 13th century, this register entry has nothing left but renamings.

issues: source: the 1864 imperial decree named it rue Gerson AND rue Restaut, which is the register's own first line; the detail gives only rue Gerson, so the reader is told the street became one thing when the source says it became two. The decree also created a place Gerson ("rue et place Gerson"). | voice: "Later identified as the rue Grenouiller or Grenouillière on Abbe Delagrive's map" imposes a date the source does not give - the register lists Delagrive last but assigns him no period.
suggested_edit: "An imperial decree of 24 August 1864 divided it into the rue Gerson and the rue Restaut." Drop "Later" before Delagrive. The 1236 and 1254 Argenteuil names and the 1443 rue aux Ecoliers de Rethel are the strongest part of this entry and should keep their room.

issues: source: "The middle section, formerly the rue Beaurepaire between the rue Dussoubs and the rue Montorgueil" is wrong - Beaurepaire is the western end, and the middle section is the rue du Renard-Saint-Sauveur, which is this card's own street. | consistency: the card is the rue du Renard-Saint-Sauveur and the detail never says what that street was; its 1313 rue Percee and 1383 rue du Renard appear only in the short description. | period: the text opens on the 1868 merger.
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Rue Greneta" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rue_Greneta&action=raw: the street "commence au 241, rue Saint-Martin et se termine au 72, rue Montorgueil", and its cross streets are listed "d'Est en Ouest" as boulevard de Sebastopol, rue de Palestro, rue Saint-Denis, rue Dussoubs. With the register's own three ranges - Greneta Saint-Martin to Saint-Denis, Renard-Saint-Sauveur Saint-Denis to Dussoubs, Beaurepaire Dussoubs to Montorgueil - the order east to west is Greneta, Renard, Beaurepaire, so the card's street is the middle one. Article cites Felix et Louis Lazare, Dictionnaire administratif et historique des rues de Paris, and Jean de La Tynna, Dictionnaire topographique... des rues de Paris, 1817.
suggested_edit: Put the card's own street first and fix the position: "Between the rue Saint-Denis and the rue Dussoubs, the street existed in 1313 as the rue Percee, then Perciee, and was the rue du Renard by 1383. In 1868 it became the middle section of the rue Greneta, with the rue Beaurepaire to the west and the old rue Greneta to the east."

issues: consistency: the card is the rue Montorgueil itself and the detail is wholly about the rue au Comte-d'Artois, the neighbouring label L0381, with no sentence saying how the two relate; the mont Orgueil the street climbs is never mentioned. | overclaim: "permanently merged" - the source says only that it was joined again in 1830.
suggested_edit: Say at the start that this is the stretch joined to the rue Montorgueil, not the rue Montorgueil itself, and drop "permanently". Better: write this card from the hill and the market and leave the Comte-d'Artois names to L0381.

issues: consistency: the card is the rue Pavee and it gets one sentence of four; the rest is the rue du Petit-Lion and the old rue Tiquetonne. The first list also drops "rue du Petit Lion" and "rue de l'Arbalete ou rue des Arbaletriers", which are in the source. | overclaim: "the rue Paule on Ducerceau's map" is fine, but see L0406 on expanding the name.
suggested_edit: Lead with the card's street: "Between the rue Dussoubs and the rue Montorgueil the street was the rue Pavee from 1313, and kept that name until 1851, when it was joined to the rue du Petit-Lion." Then the other sections briefly.

issues: consistency: the site of the hotel de Bourgogne or d'Artois, the 1543 break-up, the rue Francoise and the rue Francaise are all in the summary. The detail adds two intermediate forms, rue Neuve de Bourgogne and rue Neuve Saint-Francois, and drops 1543, which is the card's whole point - a street brand new when this sheet was cut.
suggested_edit: Return null, or keep the two new forms in a single clause and let the summary carry the rest.

issues: consistency: the summary already has the 1792 merger into the rue Montorgueil, which the detail repeats as its opening. | overclaim: "briefly returned" and "permanently reincorporated" are the detail's own judgements; the source gives only the three dates.
suggested_edit: Drop "briefly" and "permanently" and lead on the names: "The stretch between the rue Montmartre and the rue Mauconseil was first the rue Nicolas Arrode, then the rue au Comte - or a la Comtesse - d'Artois, and the rue de la Porte au Comte d'Artois."

issues: overclaim: "the eastern stretch between the rue Mondetour and the rue Saint-Denis" - the register gives no direction, and the brief warns against supplying them. | period: the text opens on the 1792-1806 Bonconseil renaming, which the summary already names.
suggested_edit: Drop "eastern" and lead on the map-relevant fact instead: "On Merian's plan the part between the rue Mondetour and the rue Saint-Denis is called the rue Saint-Jacques de l'Hopital; the street formerly ran that far."

issues: period: the only fact the detail adds to the summary is the 1936 incorporation of a section into the Halles Centrales; the oven that gave the street its name, which is what the label means, is left to the summary. | consistency (not the detail's fault, but on the same card): the short description calls Vauvilliers "the architect" - he was a Hellenist scholar who handled Paris's food supply in 1789.
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Rue Vauvilliers" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rue_Vauvilliers&action=raw: "Depuis 1864, elle tient son nom du savant helleniste Jean-Francois Vauvilliers (1737-1801)", "qui assura les approvisionnements alimentaires de Paris en 1789" - a Hellenist, not an architect. The same article has the street's own century: it "existait deja en 1238", was the "rue du Four-de-la-Couture-de-l'Eveque" in 1255, and the bishop's four banal stood "au bout de la rue du cote de l'eglise Saint-Eustache" and worked from 1137 until about 1410.
suggested_edit: Replace the 1936 sentence with the oven: "The bishop's communal oven that gave the street its name stood at the Saint-Eustache end and was in use from 1137 until about 1410, so by the time of this map the name had outlived the oven." Separately, fix "the architect Vauvilliers" in the short description.

issues: consistency: at 40 words, the floor, the entry is six spelling variants plus the two streets the absorbed section ran between; the 13th-century date, the prouvaires of Saint-Eustache and the Halles absorption are all in the summary.
suggested_edit: Return null, or cut to the three or four spellings that differ most and say nothing else.

issues: period: 36 of the entry's 50 words are a 1972 declassification for the Forum des Halles, which the summary has already covered as "the rebuilding of the Halles in the 1970s". The one new fact is the former name rue de la Ganterie.
suggested_edit: Return null, or keep one line: "It was earlier the rue de la Ganterie, the glovers' street, beside the linen market."

issues: overclaim: "the section called the rue des Bourdonnais was named after Adam Bourdon and Guillaume Bourdon" turns two attested street names into an etymology. The register says only that at the end of the 13th century it was called "rue Adam Bourdon, rue Guillaume Bourdon et rue Sire Guillaume Bourdon"; the card's own summary hedges the question - "whose name may come from a family called Bourdon" - and the detail answers it.
suggested_edit: "At the end of the 13th century it appears as the rue Adam Bourdon, the rue Guillaume Bourdon and the rue Sire Guillaume Bourdon, and as the rue des Bourdonnais from the early 14th." The 1530 rue des Etuves aux Femmes is the best fact here and should not be buried.

issues: period: the second of two sentences is an 1882 decree given with the house numbers it ran past - "about 40 metres beyond numbers 23 and 36" - which the summary has already covered as "part of it was removed in 1882". The one new fact is the 1300 name.
suggested_edit: "In 1300 it was the rue Saint-Germain a Couroiers, later simply the rue Saint-Germain or the grande rue Saint-Germain." Then stop.

issues: consistency: four of the five sentences are the rue du Battoir-Saint-Andre, a different street, on a card whose summary is only about the rue Serpente; this card is also a second label on the street L0365 covers, and the two details overlap heavily. | voice: a list of former names.
suggested_edit: Return null, or keep only the rue Serpente: the 1263 Vicus Tortuosus and the 16th-century plans that write it rue Serpente. The rue du Battoir belongs on L0365, which at least has the 1851 merger in its summary.

issues: consistency: the detail's chronology contradicts the short description above it - the summary has Guillot calling it the rue des Cordeles in 1300, the detail says it was the rue Saint-Germain before 1672 and the rue des Cordeliers only from 1672 to 1690. The register carries both and the author should have flagged the clash rather than presenting the later sequence flatly. | period: of seven dated statements, one is before 1550.
suggested_edit: Say what the register actually leaves unresolved: "Guillot already called it the rue des Cordeles in 1300, after the Franciscan convent, and in 1304 deeds name it for Saint-Come and Saint-Damien; the register then has it as the rue Saint-Germain before 1672 and the rue des Cordeliers only from 1672 to 1690." Cut the Revolution renamings and the boulevard Saint-Germain absorption.

issues: overclaim: "Henri Sauval" and "Jacques Androuet du Cerceau" - the source writes only "Sauval" and "Ducerceau", and the first names and the identification are the detail's own additions, which the brief forbids adding silently. | consistency: the card is the original rue Tiquetonne and it gets the last sentence only; the first three are the rue du Petit-Lion and the rue Pavee. The baker Roger Tiquetonne of 1399, the card's own subject, is in the summary and never picked up.
evidence: Henri Sauval (1623-1676) and Jacques Androuet du Cerceau are the usual referents, so the expansions are probably right - but they are not in the supplied register text, and the project has already been burnt by a plausible addition (quote_verification.md, the four contradicted claims). No independent source was opened to fix which Ducerceau plan the register means; the finding is that the source does not say.
suggested_edit: Write "Sauval" and "Ducerceau", as the register does, and open on the rue Tiquetonne itself: "Before the rue Etienne-Marcel was cut through, the rue Tiquetonne ran between the rue Montorgueil and the rue Montmartre; it was the rue Denis le Coffrier in 1372 and the rue Quiquetonne in 1400."

issues: overclaim: "Jacques Androuet du Cerceau recorded it as Cernelles" - the register says only "Ducerceau ecrit Cernelles"; the first names and the identification are added. | voice: the detail is a bare list of spelling variants with no statement about the street, which is what the brief's third trap warns against.
evidence: Same as L0406: the expansion is probable but is not in the supplied text, and no independent source was opened that fixes which Ducerceau the register's street entries mean. The register's own words are "Ducerceau ecrit Cernelles".
suggested_edit: Write "Ducerceau". And give the reader the street rather than the list: the source's "Cette voie existait au XIIIe siecle" and the two sections' extents carry more than six variant spellings do.

issues: period: "The section between the rue Berger and the rue de Viarmes was named rue Marie de France by municipal decision in April 2025" - a street naming from this year, 24 of the entry's 54 words, on a card about a 16th-century bathhouse street. It is the most recent fact in the whole set.
suggested_edit: Cut the 2025 sentence. What is left - rue des Etuves, rue des Estuves, and earlier the rue du Pressoir du Bret, attested in 1300 - is short but it is about the street the map shows.

issues: voice: "later Behaigne or Vieille Behaigne, references to Bohemia in 1328" reads as though something was referred to in 1328; the source means the name Behaigne, Bohemia, is attested in 1328. | consistency: the 1888 clearance for the rue du Louvre is in the summary, and the detail gives it plus the 1890 order as its closing two clauses.
suggested_edit: "...later Behaigne, from Bohemia, recorded in 1328, and Vieille Behaigne." Cut the last sentence. The 16th-century names of the Filles Repenties and the Filles Penitentes are the map-century fact here and deserve more than a clause.

issues: voice: the variant list prints "d'Autruche or d'Autruche dite du Louvre", repeating one form and dropping "de l'Autruche", which the source has between them. | consistency: the 1664 enlargement and the survival as the rue de l'Oratoire are both in the summary.
suggested_edit: "...Autheriche, then d'Autruche, de l'Autruche and d'Autruche dite du Louvre." The two dates the summary lacks - rue du Louvre in 1600, and the rue de l'Oratoire still called rue de l'Autruche in 1732 - are worth keeping and should lead.

issues: source: the extract is the register entry for the RUE DU LOUVRE, which lists what its opening suppressed, and the card is the rue des Poulies. The detail is the rue du Louvre's creation plus a 1972 renaming to rue de l'Amiral-de-Coligny; the rue des Poulies' own 1205 record and its name from a cloth-working device are in the short description and the detail never reaches them. Same case as L0328.
suggested_edit: Return null for this source. If the rue des Poulies is to have a detail it must come from its own register entry, or from Lazare, who has it under Poulies.

issues: consistency: the summary already gives the rue du Paon(-Saint-Andre) name, the 1851 renaming to rue Larrey and the destruction for the boulevard Saint-Germain; the detail adds the two boundary streets and the decree's exact date, and repeats the rest.
suggested_edit: Return null.

issues: voice: 61 words of name variants and nothing else; the chapel of Saint Mary of Egypt that the street is named after, and the corruption into Jussienne, are both in the summary and are not taken further. The 16th-century rue du Coq Heron is the one fact here worth the room.
suggested_edit: "In the 16th century it was also the rue du Coq Heron, and the rue du Coq Heron dite l'Egyptienne." Two or three earlier spellings, and no more.

issues: consistency: the card is the rue de Grenelle-Saint-Honore and the detail calls it "One section", then gives the other section equal room; the summary already has the 13th-century date and Ducerceau's "Cernelles". | voice: 47 words that are a list of variants and nothing else.
suggested_edit: Return null, or write the card's own stretch: "Running as far as the rue Coquilliere, the street appears as rue de Guernelles, Guarnelle, Guarnales and Garnelles before settling as rue de Grenelle-Saint-Honore." The rue Maverse and the rue Platriere belong to L0408.

issues: period: the closing sentence is a 1966 naming of the place Colette, on a card whose body is a good 13th-to-17th-century chain of names.
suggested_edit: Cut the 1966 sentence.

issues: period: the closing sentence is a 1965 naming of the place Paul Claudel. The body - rue de Vaulgirard 1523, chemin des Carrieres 1529, rue des Vaches 1543, chemin de Bel Ayr 1547, rue de Bel Air 1559 - is exactly the map's own decades and is the best dated series in the street set.
suggested_edit: Cut the 1965 sentence and nothing else.

issues: period: the entry opens on a 1685 widening and gives two later section names; the 14th-century existence, the only pre-1550 fact in the register, is in the summary and is stepped over.
suggested_edit: Lead on what the card is about: "The street was already there in the 14th century as the rue des Petits-Champs; the stretch between the rue Coquilliere and the place des Victoires was the rue d'Aubusson." Cut the 1685 decree.

issues: consistency: the summary already gives the 1212 rue des Chanoines, the rue Saint-Thomas-du-Louvre and the suppression for the Louvre, so the detail is largely the same four facts reordered, with 1242 and the Revolution name added. | period: three of its four statements are 1808 or later.
suggested_edit: Keep "First documented as the rue des Chanoines in 1212, it took the name rue Saint-Thomas du Louvre in 1242" and cut the rest, or return null - the register entry is five short sentences and the summary has spent most of them.

issues: period: everything in the detail is 1808 or later - the course at suppression, the pre-1808 start, the Revolution name - and the 1212 rue des Chanoines and the 1242 rue Saint-Thomas-du-Louvre, the only pre-1550 facts in the source, are left to the summary. | voice: 45 words of register administration.
suggested_edit: Lead on the two medieval names and cut the pre-1808 course: "In 1212 it was the rue des Chanoines; from 1242 it took the name of the collegiate church of Saint-Thomas-du-Louvre, which stood on it."

issues: overclaim: "According to the historian Sauval" adds a trade the register does not give, and "temporarily named it rue du Senat" adds a judgement the register does not make. | voice: "prefectural decree", as at L0367.
suggested_edit: "Sauval has it that it also bore the name rue Dauphine. A prefectoral decree of 26 February 1867 named it rue du Senat." The 1489 rue de Seine is the fact that matters.

issues: overclaim: "Bercy is shown as a feudal fortress with a donjon" drops two hedges at once - the source says the old plans show "une sorte de forteresse d'aspect feodal", a sort of fortress of feudal appearance. What the map shows is how the place looked, which is not the same as what it was.
suggested_edit: "On this map and other plans of the same years Bercy appears as a kind of fortress, feudal in look, with a keep inside a walled enclosure and a fortified gate near the Seine." Everything else in this entry is exact, including the forty horsemen and the windmill, and it is one of the best in the set.

issues: overclaim: "the village dominates the confluence of the Seine and Marne" is the detail's own reading of the sheet; the source says only what the old plans show the village to have consisted of - the church of Saint-Pierre and the remains of the Sejour de Bourgogne - and that they depict the territory schematically.
suggested_edit: "On this map the village is little more than the church of Saint-Pierre and the remains of the 14th-century Sejour de Bourgogne." The rest - 865, 1358, 11 January 1436, the Sejour du Roi with stables for fifty horses, Gillette Hennequin in 1481 - is exact and is among the best writing in the set.

issues: overclaim: "On the 1550 map, the village is shown under the spelling Iveri with its church" - the source says only "Sur un plan des annees 1550, l'eglise est presente et la commune porte alors le nom Iveri", a plan of the 1550s, unnamed. The identification with this sheet is the detail's own, and it matters: where the sources for Bercy and Bagnolet name Truschet and Hoyau outright, and the log treats that as independent corroboration, this one does not. | source: the detail puts the 52 BC battle of Lutetia at Ivry flatly, while L0444 puts it on the plain of Vitry and hedges it. The two cards cannot both be right and neither says so.
suggested_edit: "A plan of the 1550s shows the church and spells the village Iveri" - and, if the identification is to be made, make it in the sources, not in the sentence. On the battle: hedge it here as L0444 does, or drop it from one of the two cards.

issues: overclaim: "a parish survey recorded 47 households, or about 211 inhabitants" - the source says an archdeacon's visitation found the TWO parishes counting "environ 47 feux"; the detail drops "environ" from the households while keeping "about" for the inhabitants, and turns a visitation into a survey.
suggested_edit: "In 1462 an archdeacon's visitation put the two parishes at about 47 households, some 211 people." The hedge on the battle of Lutetia is well kept and the rest is exact.

issues: source: the extract supplied for this card is the article's Toponymie section plus the opening of its Prehistoire, and it breaks off mid-sentence at "Epoque gallo-romaine et haut Moyen Age". So the village's own history never reached the writer, and the card now carries seven sentences of name etymology and nothing about the place. The detail is faithful and carefully hedged throughout - "claimed", "likely confusing it", "remains debated" - and the fault is upstream, in which section was fetched.
suggested_edit: Not an edit to the text so much as a re-fetch: data/research/sources_long.csv L0445 holds 6,892 characters that end inside the sentence "L'histoire de Villejuif dans l'Antiquite et le haut Moyen Age est longtemps restee mal connue, et le demeure." Take the Histoire section from the medieval part onward and ask again.

issues: overclaim: "King Louis IX founded a Carthusian monastery here in the 13th century" - the source says only "Saint Louis y batit un monastere pour les chartreux" and gives no date; the century is supplied. The claim is also uncited in the article, and the Carthusian house Saint Louis endowed outside Paris is normally the Chartreuse de Vauvert, on the ground now under the Jardin du Luxembourg, so it is worth a second source before it is stated flatly. | voice: the source has a motte and a ROUND tower, then a square tower inside an enclosure; the detail keeps only "a fortified square tower".
evidence: On Vauvert: the Senat's own history of the Luxembourg garden and the Chartreuse's own site both place Saint Louis's Carthusian foundation at Vauvert, on the site of today's Jardin du Luxembourg, in 1257-1258 (jardin.senat.fr/en/history-heritage/history-of-the-garden.html; chartreuse.fr/en/paris-vauvert-chartreuse-site). Neither was read as a page on Gentilly, and one popular account does connect a prior of Gentilly with the Vauvert community, so this is recorded as a claim needing corroboration, NOT as a refutation.
suggested_edit: "Saint Louis built a house for the Carthusians here" - no century, until the claim is checked against Lebeuf or Lazare. And restore the round tower that preceded the square one.

issues: period: the detail is the present-day university hospital - its street number, its commune, its departement, and its place in the AP-HP - on a card about the ruined castle of Bicetre on a 1550 sheet. | source: LOG.md records that this card was "probed and skipped" because the article's history sections carry no pre-1600 reference, yet a detail written from its lead is live on the card.
evidence: LOG.md, entry of 2026-11-02 (16:10), read 3 Nov 2026: "L0447 (Bicetre) and L0467 (Auteuil) were probed and skipped: their articles' history sections carry no pre-1600 reference either." The project had already judged this source unusable for this card.
suggested_edit: Return null. The summary already says what the map shows - a ruined castle, and Louis XIII's hospital for invalid soldiers on its site.

issues: overclaim: "Charles VI also granted the nearby manor of Mallassis to his mistress Odette de Champdivers" drops the source's hedge - "Cette propriete a vraisemblablement ete donnee par Charles VI a sa maitresse". The grant is probable, not recorded.
suggested_edit: "The manor of Mallassis close by was probably given by Charles VI to his mistress Odette de Champdivers." Everything else here is exact, including "Les Brieres sur le plan", which the source itself supplies - this is the strongest entry in the village set.

issues: source: the detail makes Humbert II de Viennois, patriarch of Alexandria, the man John the Good promised the castle to in 1359, and then "Humbert de la Tour-du-Pin" the owner in the 16th century - two owners two centuries apart. They are one man, and he died in 1355. The register's own entry is impossible on both counts and the detail passes it on, split in two; this is the Mathoniere case again (quote_verification.md, contradicted claim 4).
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Humbert II de Viennois" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Humbert_II_de_Viennois&action=raw: the article's subject is "Humbert de la Tour-du-Pin", known "sous le nom de Humbert II de Viennois", "le dernier dauphin de Viennois", born 1312 at La Tour-du-Pin, "Nomme patriarche d'Alexandrie le 31 janvier 1351", died "22 mai 1355" at Clermont. One man, dead four years before the 1359 promise and two centuries before the 16th-century ownership.
suggested_edit: Delete both sentences until the source is replaced. The Templar grant of 1152 by Mathieu de Beaumont, the passage to the Hospitallers, and Dagobert's repudiation of Gomatrude in 629 - which the detail rightly hedges as tradition - carry this card without them.

issues: overclaim: "By 1550, a cluster of about fifteen houses had formed the hamlet" - the source says "Cent cinquante ans plus tard, le carrefour s'est garni d'une quinzaine de maisons", a hundred and fifty years after the manor of about 1400. The date is the author's arithmetic presented as a record, and it lands on the one year ingest_detail.py's year check waives as the sheet's own date, so nothing would have caught it.
suggested_edit: "A century and a half later the crossroads had gathered some fifteen houses, the first hamlet of Popincourt, just outside the wall of Charles V." The 1561 Reformed temple and its destruction the next year are exact and are the best thing in the entry.

issues: overclaim: "establishing La Courtille as a famous suburban entertainment district" - "quartier de divertissement" is the source's own phrase, but "famous" is not; the only "celebre" in the source is in a footnote about the Douanier Rousseau.
suggested_edit: "...and La Courtille became a quarter of amusements." The guinguet and the guinguettes, and why the wine was cheap outside the wall, are exactly right for this card.

issues: voice: "the Catholic League leveled the mills, houses, and the church" - US spelling, and one the US_SPELLINGS table in scripts/ingest_detail.py does not cover, so the check passed it. | period: the earliest date in the text is November 1562, twelve years after the map; the Villeneuve-sur-Gravois as the sheet shows it gets nothing. The source is only 1,365 characters and opens in the 17th century, so this is a source limit rather than a choice.
suggested_edit: "levelled". And add "levelled" (with "labelled", already there) to US_SPELLINGS, which catches "labeled" and "canceled" but not this one.

issues: overclaim: "The hamlet's name comes from Clenini Curtis, named after a Gallo-Roman villa owner" drops both the attribution and the conditional - the source reads "D'apres l'Abbe Lebeuf, son nom PROVIENDRAIT de Clenini Curtis ... du nom d'un certain Cleninus, proprietaire d'une villa gallo-romaine, decouverte en 1738".
suggested_edit: "The Abbe Lebeuf derived the name from Clenini Curtis, after a Cleninus whose Gallo-Roman villa was found here in 1738." The 9 September 1465 vintage, taken from Jean de Roye's chronicle, is the best sentence in the whole village set.

issues: source: the article dates the move from the abbaye d'en haut to the abbaye d'en bas both 1686 and 1685, in two different passages; the detail takes 1686 and says nothing of the clash, which the brief asks to put in notes.
suggested_edit: Either hedge - "in the 1680s the nuns left the upper convent" - or keep 1686 and flag the article's own inconsistency. The 1590 siege and Henri IV's batteries are the best thing in this entry and are exactly right for a card about the hill in 1550.

issues: conflation: "The fief covered 58 hectares of marshland that King Louis VII granted to the canons of Sainte-Opportune in 1153" welds two separate statements - the fief's 58 hectares from the Champs-Elysees to the chemin de Montmartre, and the 1153 grant of the marshes between the butte Montmartre and the Seine as far as Chaillot. The source does not say they are the same land. | source: the 58-hectare sentence carries no citation in the article. | overclaim: "the bishopric of Paris" where the source says "l'archeveche de Paris".
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Ferme de la Grange-Bateliere" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ferme_de_la_Grange-Bateli%C3%A8re&action=raw: "Le fief de la Grange Bateliere s'etendait sur 58 hectares des Champs-Elysees au chemin de Montmartre" stands in the paragraph on the fief's extent and has no footnote; the grant is a separate sentence, "En 1153, Louis VII le Jeune donne aux chanoines de l'eglise Sainte-Opportune les marais qui s'etendent entre la butte-Montmartre et la Seine, jusqu'a Chaillot", footnoted to "Le fief de la Grange-Bateliere" on Gallica. Ownership is footnoted to Maurice Dumoulin, Etudes de topographie parisienne, t. II, 1930, p. 145.
suggested_edit: Split the two: "The fief ran to 58 hectares, from the Champs-Elysees to the chemin de Montmartre. In 1153 Louis VII had granted the canons of Sainte-Opportune the marshes between the butte Montmartre and the Seine." And "archbishopric", not "bishopric", if the source's word is kept.

issues: period: every date in the text is 1622-1689; the map shows the faubourg in 1550 and nothing in the detail is about it. | source: the article has no content at all before 1600 - its Historique opens "Le faubourg Saint-Germain s'urbanise au cours des XVIIe et XVIIIe siecles" - so no faithful detail from this source can be about the map's century. | overclaim: the source dates the faubourg's rise to the fashionable quarter to the early 18th century and the Regence, not to the Pont Royal; the detail moves it some thirty years earlier and adds "rapidly".
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Faubourg Saint-Germain" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Faubourg_Saint-Germain&action=raw: the earliest date in the article is 1622, and on the Marais it says "Cette tendance se renforce au debut du XVIIIe siecle, notamment durant la Regence" ... "devient le quartier a la mode, le << noble faubourg >>, alors que le quartier du Marais amorce son declin" - a different moment from the 1685-1689 Pont Royal the detail ties it to.
suggested_edit: Return null for this source, or source the card afresh (the abbey's bourg, the Pre-aux-Clercs, the foire Saint-Germain) - the article behind it begins in the 17th century. If it must ship, at minimum: "...favoured building along the rue de l'Universite and the rue de Grenelle; the faubourg became the fashionable quarter in the early 18th century, as the Marais began to decline."

issues: source: "the name faubourg Saint-Honore was applied to the stretch outside the wall as far as the Grand Egout" reverses the source, which has the street running as far as the faubourg du Roule AFTER crossing the Grand Egout. | overclaim: "local resistance and the city's outward expansion forced the crown to extend the building limits in 1740 and 1765" supplies a cause the source does not state - it reports the protest and the moved limits as separate facts. | overclaim: the name was restricted from 1633, not 1631; 1631 is the gate's rebuilding, and the detail merges the two and loses 1633. | period: only the first sentence is before 1550, and the text closes on Empress Eugenie and a missing house number 13.
evidence: The supplied source_fr (fr.wikipedia, "Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honore", Historique) reads: "A partir de 1633, cette appellation est reservee a la rue situee a l'ouest de la nouvelle porte Saint-Honore reconstruite en 1631 ... et qui va jusqu'au faubourg du Roule apres avoir traverse le Grand Egout, qui se situait approximativement au carrefour avec la rue du Colisee", and "les habitants du faubourg Saint-Honore s'insurgent et reclament un traitement privilegie" followed separately by "La limite d'interdiction de batir est reportee en 1740 ... et, le 10 fevrier 1765, jusqu'a la rue de Chaillot". The article's references for this stretch are E.-T. Lemaire, "Le developpement du faubourg Saint-Honore au XVIIIe siecle", Bulletin de la Societe historique de Paris et de l'Ile-de-France, 1957-1959, and Arch. nat., K 982.
suggested_edit: Fix the course - "as far as the faubourg du Roule, beyond the Grand Egout" - give 1633 for the name and 1631 for the gate, drop "forced", and cut the Eugenie sentence. Then the card still needs a pre-1550 source: all this source has for the map's century is the medieval road from the church of Saint-Honore to the pont du Roule.

issues: source: "a church dedicated to Saint Mary Magdalene, which was rebuilt in 1429" rests on a date that appears in this article and nowhere else the project holds - the article devoted to that church gives 1238, 1366 and 1492 and never 1429, and the Le Roule article in this same corpus says 1492 and 1660. One of the three is wrong and the detail picked the uncorroborated one. | period: the back half is 1613, 1659 and 1722, while the article's 14th-century material - the bishop's couture in two parts, the Port-l'Eveque, the comparison with Saint-Germain-des-Pres - goes unused.
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Ancienne eglise de la Madeleine" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ancienne_%C3%A9glise_de_la_Madeleine&action=raw: a chapel "attestee depuis 1238" (Antoine Krieger, La Madeleine, 1937, p. 28), "restauree en 1366" by Jean Le Coq (Krieger, p. 27), a new chapel to sainte Madeleine "adjointe en 1492 a l'eglise existante" with its first stone laid by Charles VIII (Krieger, p. 39), and the new building's first stone laid "le 7 juillet 1659" (Krieger, p. 37). No 1429 anywhere. Within this project's own corpus, the Le Roule source (L0465) says the church was "reconstruite en 1492 et 1660", and the Ville l'Eveque source says "reconstruite en 1429" - and the dedicated article dates the 1492 work as an addition to the existing church, not a rebuilding.
suggested_edit: Drop "which was rebuilt in 1429" until one of the three dates is settled from Krieger or Lazare. Replace the 1613 and 1659 sentences with the 14th-century couture: the bishop's land in two parts, one along the Seine served by the Port-l'Eveque, the other north of the chemin du Roule between the portes Saint-Honore and Montmartre - the Right Bank's answer to the faubourg Saint-Germain-des-Pres.
